items.title: RidgeCV alpha for the physchem base
items.spec: In fit_predict, replace Ridge(alpha=1.0) on the standardized physchem features with RidgeCV(alphas=np.logspace(-2, 3, 12)) fit on the training fold only. Keep everything else unchanged: the base prediction is still base_tr and base_te, and the two-stage XGBoost residual model is trained on y - base_tr. The alpha is chosen by RidgeCV's internal generalized cross-validation, so no test data is used.

items.title: Spline-expanded physchem base
items.spec: Replace the physchem Ridge base with a spline basis. Standardize the seven physchem features (TPSA, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, MolWt, NumRotatableBonds, aromatic fraction), then apply sklearn SplineTransformer(n_knots=4, degree=3, include_bias=False) fit on the training fold. Fit Ridge(alpha=3.0) on the spline features to get base_tr and base_te. The XGBoost two-stage residual model is unchanged and is trained on y - base_tr.

items.title: Physchem base prediction as an XGBoost input feature
items.spec: Keep the two-stage XGBoost recipe, but also append the out-of-fold base prediction as one extra column of Xtr and Xte. Use 5-fold KFold(shuffle=True, random_state=seed) on the training fold to produce out-of-fold base predictions for Xtr, and fit the base on the full training fold for Xte. Still fit the residual target y - base_tr, so the base is both an input and an offset. This lets trees learn where the linear base is over- or under-confident.

items.title: Importance-based feature pruning before the residual boosters
items.spec: Before the two-stage XGBoost fit, fit a quick stage-1 squared-error XGBoost on the full feature matrix with 150 rounds. Keep only the columns whose total gain importance is in the top 400 (use get_booster().get_score(importance_type='total_gain') and map names back to column indices). Train both stage 1 and stage 2 on the reduced matrix. Feature selection uses training labels only, and it is done inside fit_predict on each fold.

items.title: Clip predictions to the training target range
items.spec: After computing the final prediction base_te + stage2.predict(Xte), clip the returned array to [min(y) - 0.1*r, max(y) + 0.1*r], where r = max(y) - min(y) and y is the training fold target. This prevents extreme extrapolation for out-of-domain molecules, where the linear physchem base can give unrealistic values. Change nothing else.

items.title: Stage-1 learning-rate and round pairing
items.spec: In the two-stage XGBoost recipe, change only the stage-1 squared-error model. Use learning_rate=0.06 with n_estimators=100 instead of learning_rate=0.03 with 200 rounds. Keep stage 2 at 400 L1 rounds with learning_rate=0.03, so the stage-1 contribution is roughly half of its current total shrinkage. The goal is to test whether a shorter squared-error warm start helps the L1 stage.

items.title: Leave-self-out Tanimoto nearest-neighbour target feature
items.spec: Compute the Morgan bit fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits) for the training and test molecules, and their pairwise Tanimoto similarity. For each test molecule, take the mean target of its k=5 most similar training molecules and append it as one feature column. For training molecules, compute the same feature with the self-match excluded, so there is no target leakage. Append this column to Xtr and Xte, then run the unchanged two-stage XGBoost recipe.

items.title: Drop the full RDKit descriptor block from the residual features
items.spec: In featurize_one, keep only the 2048 Morgan count features and the six physchem values already used by the base. Remove the full Descriptors.descList block (about 200 columns) from the XGBoost input matrix. The Ridge base and the two-stage XGBoost recipe are otherwise unchanged. The goal is to test whether the full descriptor set adds noise to the boosted residual model, and to cut feature computation time.

items.title: Down-weight large molecules in the L1 stage
items.spec: In stage 2 only, pass sample_weight to XGBRegressor.fit. Set w = 1/sqrt(n_heavy_atoms), normalized so that mean(w) = 1, where n_heavy_atoms is each training molecule's heavy-atom count, computed with rdkit. Stage 1 and the ridge base are unchanged. The aim is to stop the L1 residual fit from being dominated by the largest molecules, which may be least representative of the small-molecule test distribution.

items.title: Shallow gradient-boosted physchem base instead of Ridge
items.spec: Replace the Ridge physchem base with a shallow XGBoost base. Fit XGBRegressor(max_depth=2, n_estimators=150, learning_rate=0.05, subsample=0.8, objective='reg:absoluteerror', random_state=seed, n_jobs=8) on the seven unscaled physchem features, using the training fold only, to get base_tr and base_te. Keep the two-stage Morgan-plus-descriptor XGBoost residual model on y - base_tr unchanged, so the first stage has the same offset form as now.

items.title: Tanimoto-kernel SVR ensemble member
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, compute Morgan count fingerprints (radius 2, 2048 bits) for train and test, then fit sklearn SVR with a precomputed Tanimoto (min-max / Jaccard for counts) kernel K(a,b)=sum(min(a,b))/sum(max(a,b)) on the training residuals y - base_tr, with C=1.0 and epsilon=0.05. Predict the test residuals from the test-vs-train kernel. Final output is base_te + 0.5*xgb_pred + 0.5*svr_pred, i.e. average the existing XGBoost residual prediction with the SVR residual prediction. Use seed nowhere in SVR since it is deterministic.

items.title: LightGBM residual model averaged with XGBoost
items.spec: Keep the Ridge baseline and the two-stage XGBoost residual model as they are. Add a LightGBM regressor (objective='l1', n_estimators=600, learning_rate=0.03, num_leaves=31, min_child_samples=10, colsample_bytree=0.3, subsample=0.8, subsample_freq=1, random_state=seed, n_jobs=8, verbose=-1) fit on the same features and the same residual target y - base_tr. Return base_te plus the simple average of the XGBoost stage2 prediction and the LightGBM prediction.

items.title: Add MACCS keys and FCFP-style feature-invariant fingerprints
items.spec: Extend featurize_one so the feature vector also contains the 167 MACCS keys (rdMACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys converted to numpy) and a feature-invariant Morgan count fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator with atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen(), radius 2, 1024 bits). Concatenate these after the existing Morgan count bits and descriptors. Everything else in fit_predict stays identical.

items.title: Robust linear baseline with quantile-transformed physchem features
items.spec: Replace the Ridge baseline in fit_predict with a more robust pipeline: fit sklearn QuantileTransformer(n_quantiles=min(200, len(train)), output_distribution='normal') on the six physchem descriptors plus aromatic fraction (the phys() output), then fit HuberRegressor(epsilon=1.35, alpha=1e-3, max_iter=1000) on the transformed features to predict y. Use the fitted model's predictions as base_tr and base_te in place of the Ridge predictions, leaving the XGBoost residual stages unchanged.

items.title: Stronger regularization of the XGBoost residual stages
items.spec: Keep the feature set, Ridge baseline and two-stage structure. Change the XGBoost hyperparameters to reduce overfitting on only 728 molecules: max_depth=4, min_child_weight=5, reg_lambda=5.0, reg_alpha=0.1, gamma=0.1, subsample=0.7, colsample_bytree=0.2. Keep learning_rate=0.03 and the stage1 squared-error and stage2 absolute-error objectives as they are.

items.title: Inner scaffold-grouped early stopping for the boosting rounds
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, split the training molecules into 4 folds grouped by Murcko scaffold (MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, group by the scaffold string, assign whole groups to folds with a seeded shuffle). Use the first inner fold as a validation set for stage2 only: train stage1 and stage2 with an eval_set on the validation residuals, early_stopping_rounds=50, and n_estimators up to 1000 for stage2, then refit on all training data with the best iteration count (best_iteration+1 rounds). Keep the objectives and other parameters unchanged.

items.title: Seed bagging of the boosted residual model
items.spec: Keep the features, Ridge baseline and two-stage XGBoost structure. In fit_predict, train the two-stage model 5 times with seeds seed*10+k for k in 0..4 (different subsample and colsample draws, each with the same hyperparameters), and average the 5 stage2 test predictions before adding base_te. This reduces variance from the stochastic subsampling; keep the total runtime well under the 10-minute job limit.

items.title: Tanimoto nearest-neighbour residual correction
items.spec: After computing the XGBoost residual prediction, compute the Jaccard similarity between each test molecule's Morgan bit vector (radius 2, 2048 bits) and all training molecules' bit vectors. For each test molecule take the k=5 most similar training molecules, weight them by similarity raised to power 2, and compute a weighted average of their out-of-model residuals (y - base_tr - in-sample stage2 prediction on train). Add this kNN residual correction, scaled by 0.3, to the final prediction. Use the same procedure for train residuals only through the stored training values; no leakage across the test set.

items.title: Log-target sanity transform and prediction clipping
items.spec: Keep the entire pipeline unchanged, but wrap it so the final predictions are clipped to the range [min(train_y) - 0.2*range, max(train_y) + 0.2*range], where range = max(train_y) - min(train_y). Also apply an explicit mean-centering: subtract np.median(train_y) from y before fitting the Ridge baseline and add it back to the final output, so the boosted models see a zero-median target. This guards against extrapolation on unusual test molecules.

items.title: Pseudo-Huber stage two
items.spec: In fit_predict, replace the stage-2 XGBRegressor objective 'reg:absoluteerror' with 'reg:pseudohubererror' (huber_slope=0.5), keeping n_estimators=400 and the xgb_model=stage1.get_booster() continuation. Everything else stays unchanged. Pseudo-Huber has a smooth gradient near zero, which may give steadier leaf values than pure L1.

items.title: Stage round counts 300/300
items.spec: Change the two-stage recipe so stage1 uses n_estimators=300 (squared error) and stage2 uses n_estimators=300 (absolute error) with continuation from stage1. Keep all other params the same. This tests whether more L2 warm-up and fewer L1 rounds helps.

items.title: Stronger XGB regularization
items.spec: Add reg_lambda=5, reg_alpha=0.5, gamma=0.05 and min_child_weight=5 to the shared XGBoost params dict (both stages). Keep everything else the same. This tests stronger leaf and split regularization for the small dataset.

items.title: Seed-bagged two-stage model
items.spec: Wrap the two-stage XGB fit in a loop over 3 seeds (seed, seed+1, seed+2), each with its own random_state and subsample=0.7. Average the three stage2 predictions and add base_te. Keep n_jobs=8. Only the XGB part is repeated. The physchem ridge is fit once.

items.title: Ionization and polarity ridge features
items.spec: Add features to phys_one for the ridge base: formal charge sum, counts of carboxylic acid, basic amine and amide SMARTS matches, fraction of sp3 carbons (rdMolDescriptors.CalcFractionCSP3), and number of rings. Use Chem.MolFromSmarts patterns compiled once at module level. Keep Ridge alpha=1.0 on the standardized features, so the residual booster sees a better base.

items.title: kNN residual correction
items.spec: After computing the final prediction, compute Tanimoto similarity on binary Morgan bits between each test molecule and the training molecules. Use the training residuals (y minus in-sample base plus stage predictions is overfit, so use y - base_tr instead of the boosted residuals). For each test molecule take the similarity-weighted mean of that residual over the top 5 neighbors with similarity above 0.5, shrink it by 0.3, and add it to the prediction. Leave molecules with no such neighbors unchanged.

items.title: Rank-Gaussian target transform
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, map y to normal scores with scipy.stats.rankdata and norm.ppf((rank-0.5)/n), then rescale to the original mean and sd. Fit the ridge and XGB on the transformed target. Map the predictions back by interpolating np.interp against the sorted transformed values and sorted original y. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

items.title: Drop rare fingerprint bits
items.spec: After featurizing the train set, compute for each Morgan count column the number of training molecules with a nonzero value. Keep only the columns with count of at least 5 (all descriptor columns are kept). Apply the same column mask to the test features. Fit both XGB stages on the reduced matrix, which cuts noise columns and lets colsample_bytree=0.3 select better.

items.title: Learning-rate 0.02 with more rounds
items.spec: Set learning_rate=0.02 in the shared params, stage1 n_estimators=300 and stage2 n_estimators=600. Keep everything else unchanged. This tests a slower shrinkage within the two-stage recipe.

items.title: Trimmed refit after residual screening
items.spec: After the current two-stage fit, compute in-sample absolute residuals on the training set. Drop the 5% of training molecules with the largest errors and refit stage1 and stage2 on the remaining molecules with the same params. Predict with the refit model. The ridge base stays fit on all the data.

items.title: Descriptor-only features
items.spec: In featurize_one, drop the Morgan count fingerprint and keep only the RDKit descriptor vector (Descriptors.descList). Caco-2 permeability is driven by physchem properties (TPSA, logP, HBD, etc.), and fingerprint bits may not generalize across unseen scaffolds. Keep the rest of the pipeline unchanged.

items.title: Add MACCS keys and reduce Morgan bits
items.spec: Append MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys converted to a numpy array) to the features, and cut Morgan fpSize from 2048 to 512. This gives a more compact, generalizable substructure representation alongside the descriptors.

items.title: Huber-style single-stage XGB
items.spec: Replace the two-stage XGB (squared error then absolute error warm start) with a single XGBRegressor using objective 'reg:pseudohubererror' (huber_slope=0.5) and 500 trees on y - base_tr. This tests whether the warm-start complexity is needed.

items.title: Add CatBoost to ensemble
items.spec: Train a CatBoostRegressor (loss_function MAE, depth 6, iterations 800, learning_rate 0.05, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0) on the same features and residual target y - base_tr. Average its prediction with the XGB prediction 50/50 and add base_te.

items.title: Stronger linear base with more physchem
items.spec: Extend phys_one with extra descriptors (NumAromaticRings, FractionCSP3, HeavyAtomCount, RingCount, MolMR, LabuteASA, charge-related counts such as the number of carboxylic acids and basic amines via SMARTS) and use RidgeCV with alphas 0.1 to 100 for the base model. A better base lets the trees fit a smaller residual.

items.title: Stronger XGB regularization
items.spec: Set max_depth=4, min_child_weight=5, reg_lambda=5, colsample_bytree=0.2, and subsample=0.7 in params. With only about 580 training molecules per fold and unseen scaffolds, shallower and more regularized trees may generalize better.

items.title: Seed-bagged XGB
items.spec: Wrap the two XGB stages in a loop over 5 different seeds (seed*10+i) and average the stage2 predictions. This reduces variance from subsampling and column sampling. Reduce n_jobs overhead if needed to stay under the time limit.

items.title: Feature selection by variance and importance
items.spec: After featurizing, remove the fingerprint columns that are nonzero in fewer than 10 training molecules, and drop constant descriptors. Fit on the training set only. This reduces noise features so colsample picks more informative columns.

items.title: Add Morgan with chirality-free feature invariants and atom pair counts
items.spec: Add count-based atom-pair fingerprints (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator, fpSize 1024) to the feature vector. These capture topological distances between pharmacophore-like atoms, which is complementary to the Morgan environments.

items.title: Lower learning rate with more trees
items.spec: Change learning_rate to 0.015 and double the n_estimators (stage1 400, stage2 800) to get smoother boosting. Check that the run time stays within budget.

items.title: Seed-averaged two-stage XGBoost
items.spec: Keep everything in fit_predict as it is (ridge physchem base, Morgan counts + RDKit descriptors, stage1 200 rounds reg:squarederror then stage2 400 rounds reg:absoluteerror warm-started from stage1), but instead of fitting one two-stage model, fit 5 independent copies with random_state = seed, seed+1, ..., seed+4 and also vary subsample/colsample row-column draws only through that seed (no other parameter changes). Average the 5 test predictions with the mean, then add the ridge base prediction. Reduce n_jobs to 8 still (XGBoost handles the threads; the models are fit sequentially). This is pure variance reduction on the exact incumbent recipe, which single-seed bagging experiments hinted at (-0.0035) but never combined with the two-stage fit. Keep runtime in check: 5 x 600 rounds on ~580 training rows is still well under the 10-minute budget.

items.title: Rebalance the two boosting stages
items.spec: The incumbent fits 200 squared-error rounds then 400 absolute-error rounds, both at learning_rate 0.03. Change only the schedule: use learning_rate 0.02 with 300 squared-error rounds for stage 1 and 700 absolute-error rounds for stage 2 (same warm start via xgb_model=stage1.get_booster(), same depth/subsample/colsample/min_child_weight). The intent is to test whether the accepted two-stage gain is sensitive to how much of the total shrinkage is spent on L2 versus L1; a longer, slower L1 tail should fit the median more carefully without over-fitting because the L2 stage has already captured the smooth trend. Nothing else in the file changes.

items.title: Pseudo-Huber second stage
items.spec: Replace the stage-2 objective 'reg:absoluteerror' with 'reg:pseudohubererror' and set huber_slope=0.5 (roughly a third of the target's spread, so most residuals sit in the quadratic region and only outliers are down-weighted linearly). Keep stage 1 (200 rounds reg:squarederror) and the warm start unchanged, keep n_estimators=400 and all other parameters identical. The evaluation metric is MAE, but a smooth loss gives better-behaved gradients than the constant +/-1 of L1 while still being robust, so this directly tests whether the accepted L1 stage is winning through robustness or through exact median targeting.

items.title: Ionization and polarity features in the ridge base
items.spec: Extend phys_one, which currently returns TPSA, MolLogP, NumHDonors, NumHAcceptors, MolWt, NumRotatableBonds and the aromatic-atom fraction, with five cheap ionization/polarity terms computed from the same molecule: (1) count of carboxylic-acid matches via SMARTS '[CX3](=O)[OX2H1]', (2) count of basic amine matches via SMARTS '[NX3;H2,H1;!$(N[#6]=[O,N,S])]', (3) formal charge sum from Chem.GetFormalCharge, (4) Descriptors.NumAromaticRings, (5) Descriptors.FractionCSP3. Cache compiled SMARTS patterns at module level. Everything downstream is unchanged: StandardScaler, Ridge(alpha=1.0), then the two-stage XGBoost on the residuals. Permeability is dominated by ionization state at physiological pH, which neither logP nor TPSA alone encodes, so the linear base is the right place for these.

items.title: Tanimoto k-nearest-neighbour residual correction
items.spec: After computing the final prediction (ridge base + two-stage XGBoost residual), add a small nearest-neighbour correction. Compute 2048-bit Morgan bit vectors for train and test, get the Tanimoto similarity of each test molecule to all training molecules, and take its k=5 most similar training molecules. Obtain out-of-fold training residuals by running an inner 5-fold KFold (shuffled with the given seed) over the same full pipeline is too slow, so instead use the in-bag residuals from a single extra XGBoost fit with subsample=0.7 and use only out-of-bag-like shrinkage: multiply the correction by 0.3. Concretely, correction_i = 0.3 * sum_j w_ij * r_j / sum_j w_ij over the k neighbours, where w_ij is the Tanimoto similarity and r_j is the training residual y_j - (base_j + stage2 prediction on train). Add the correction to the test prediction. Keep the shrinkage factor 0.3 fixed so the change cannot do much damage.

items.title: Inner scaffold-grouped CV for the number of L1 rounds
items.spec: Choose the stage-2 round count per fold instead of hard-coding 400. Inside fit_predict, split the training set with GroupKFold(n_splits=4) using Murcko scaffold strings (Chem.Scaffolds.MurckoScaffold.MurckoScaffoldSmiles, falling back to the SMILES itself when it returns an empty string) as groups. For each inner split, run the full recipe (ridge base, stage-1 200 squared-error rounds, then stage-2 L1) and record the inner-validation MAE after 100, 200, 400, 600 and 800 stage-2 rounds using a single fit with staged evaluation (fit 800 rounds once, then predict with iteration_range). Average the MAE curve over the 4 inner folds, pick the round count with the lowest mean, and refit on the full training set with that value. Keep every other hyper-parameter fixed.

items.title: Avalon and ErG fingerprints inside the two-stage recipe
items.spec: Append two extra fingerprint blocks to featurize_one, which currently returns Morgan counts (2048) concatenated with the full RDKit descriptor list: the Avalon count fingerprint (rdkit.Avalon.pyAvalonTools.GetAvalonCountFP with nBits=512, converted to a dense float32 array) and the ErG pharmacophore fingerprint (rdkit.Chem.rdReducedGraphs.GetErGFingerprint, 315 floats). Cache them in the same _CACHE entry. The model and the ridge base stay exactly as they are. This combination scored 0.3710 against the older single-stage incumbent, i.e. a small apparent gain that was never retested on top of the accepted two-stage residual fit, so this slot is specifically about whether the two effects add.

items.title: Stronger leaf and split regularization
items.spec: Keep the architecture and the two-stage schedule exactly as they are, and change only the regularization terms in the shared params dict: set min_child_weight=6 (from 3), gamma=0.5 (new, minimum loss reduction per split), reg_lambda=5.0 (from the default 1.0) and max_depth=5 (from 6). With only ~580 training molecules per fold and scaffold-disjoint test folds, the incumbent trees are likely splitting on fingerprint bits that are present in a handful of molecules; harder split acceptance and heavier leaf shrinkage should trade a little training fit for generalization to unseen skeletons. Everything else, including the 200 + 400 round split and learning_rate 0.03, is unchanged.

items.title: Similarity-gated shrinkage toward the ridge base
items.spec: Make the boosted residual correction depend on how well the test molecule is covered by the training set. Compute Morgan bit vectors and, for each test molecule, its maximum Tanimoto similarity s to any training molecule. Define a gate g = clip((s - 0.2) / 0.3, 0.0, 1.0), so molecules with max similarity at or below 0.2 get g=0 and those at or above 0.5 get g=1. Return base_te + g * stage2.predict(Xte) instead of base_te + stage2.predict(Xte). For far-out-of-domain scaffolds the fingerprint-driven correction is mostly noise and the smooth physchem ridge is the safer predictor, which matters here because every fold tests on unseen skeletons. Keep the two thresholds fixed at 0.2 and 0.5; no tuning inside the fold.

items.title: Ring-system and scaffold-topology features in the ridge base
items.spec: Add six whole-molecule topology descriptors to phys_one, which currently returns seven values: number of rings (rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumRings), number of aromatic rings, number of saturated rings, number of bridgehead atoms (CalcNumBridgeheadAtoms), number of spiro atoms (CalcNumSpiroAtoms), and the fraction of heavy atoms that belong to the Murcko scaffold (heavy atoms of MurckoScaffold.GetScaffoldForMol divided by total heavy atoms, 0.0 when the scaffold is empty). Standardize and fit Ridge(alpha=1.0) on the 13 features as before, then run the unchanged two-stage XGBoost on the residuals. Rigid, highly fused ring systems permeate differently from flexible chains, and the current base has only NumRotatableBonds and aromatic fraction to express that.

items.title: Average XGB with a CatBoost model on the same residual
items.spec: Keep the Ridge baseline and the two-stage XGB. Also fit a CatBoostRegressor (loss_function='MAE', iterations=1500, learning_rate=0.03, depth=6, rsm=0.2, random_seed=seed, thread_count=8, verbose=0) on Xtr against the residual y - base_tr. Return base_te + 0.5*xgb_pred + 0.5*cat_pred.

items.title: Seed-bagged XGB ensemble
items.spec: Wrap the stage1+stage2 XGB fit in a loop over 5 sub-seeds (seed*10+k, k=0..4). Pass each sub-seed as random_state to both stages. Average the 5 stage2 predictions on Xte and add base_te. All other parameters stay the same.

items.title: Add RDKit 2D pharmacophore/MACCS and atom-pair count features
items.spec: In featurize_one, also compute MACCS keys (rdkit.Chem.MACCSkeys.GenMACCSKeys, converted to a numpy array of 167 bits) and an atom-pair count fingerprint (rdFingerprintGenerator.GetAtomPairGenerator(fpSize=1024).GetCountFingerprintAsNumPy). Concatenate them to the existing fp+desc vector. The model is unchanged.

items.title: Drop Morgan bits seen in fewer than 3 training molecules
items.spec: Inside fit_predict, after building Xtr and Xte, compute for the first N_BITS columns (the Morgan counts) how many training rows are nonzero. Keep only the Morgan columns that are nonzero in at least 3 training molecules, and keep all descriptor columns. Apply the same column mask to Xte before the XGB fits.

items.title: Lower XGB colsample and add L1/L2 regularization
items.spec: In params, change colsample_bytree from 0.3 to 0.15. Add reg_lambda=5.0 and reg_alpha=0.5. Also change subsample from 0.8 to 0.7. Leave everything else unchanged.

items.title: Longer MAE stage with lower learning rate
items.spec: Set learning_rate to 0.02 for both stages. Change stage1 n_estimators to 300 and stage2 n_estimators to 800. Everything else stays the same.

items.title: Pseudo-Huber objective for stage 2
items.spec: Replace stage2's objective='reg:absoluteerror' with objective='reg:pseudohubererror' and huber_slope=0.5. Keep warm-starting from stage1 and n_estimators=400. This gives a smoother robust loss than pure MAE.

items.title: Richer linear baseline with more descriptors
items.spec: In phys_one, add these descriptors to vals: Descriptors.FractionCSP3, Descriptors.NumAromaticRings, Descriptors.HeavyAtomCount, Descriptors.NumHeteroatoms, rdMolDescriptors.CalcNumAmideBonds (import from rdkit.Chem), plus a formal-charge count (the number of atoms with nonzero GetFormalCharge) and the count of carboxylic acid groups, matched with the SMARTS 'C(=O)[OH]'. Raise the Ridge alpha to 3.0.

items.title: Blend in an RBF-kernel SVR on scaled descriptors
items.spec: Also fit sklearn SVR(kernel='rbf', C=3.0, epsilon=0.05, gamma='scale') on the descriptor part of Xtr (the columns after N_BITS). Standardize these columns with a StandardScaler fit on train, then clip them to [-5,5]. Fit the SVR against the residual y - base_tr. Final prediction: base_te + 0.7*xgb_pred + 0.3*svr_pred.

items.title: Morgan radius 3 with feature-invariant (FCFP) counts added
items.spec: Keep the ECFP counts at radius 2. Also add a second Morgan count fingerprint built with rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganGenerator(radius=3, fpSize=1024, atomInvariantsGenerator=rdFingerprintGenerator.GetMorganFeatureAtomInvGen()). Concatenate it in featurize_one before the descriptors. The model is unchanged.
